sections.h2: Jeff Davis County at a glance
sections.html:
Jeff Davis County is farm and timber country in southeast Georgia. Hazlehurst is the seat and the largest community, and Denton is the only other city. The county has an estimated 15,219 residents as of July 2025, up 3.0% from the 2020 count of 14,779.

Homes are inexpensive here. The middle value of an owner-occupied home is $118,300 for 2020-2024, and 71.3% of homes are lived in by their owners. Only nine building permits were issued in 2025, so new construction barely competes with resales. A seller mostly faces other older houses, and buyers tend to be local people who already know the area. A house in Hazlehurst, a country place near a crossroads and a cut-over timber tract each draw a different buyer, so price each one on its own comparable sales.

sections.h2: Who to call about Jeff Davis County property tax
sections.html:
Start at the Tax Commissioner, 14 Jeff Davis Street, Suite 104, Hazlehurst, GA 31539, telephone (912) 375-6622. Mail goes to PO Box 558, and weekday service ends at 4:30. An online payment portal also exists. If a deadline is close, ask the office which payment method is safest before you mail a check.

  • Tax Commissioner: sends and collects bills, hands out mobile home decals, and also takes timber, heavy duty equipment and intangible tax
  • Tax Assessor, (912) 375-6624: sets values and receives appeals
  • Board of Equalization: the Grand Jury names its members to rule on value disputes
  • County commission and school board: choose the millage rates

The commissioner has no say over how much your house is worth or what the millage rate is. A complaint about value goes to the assessor.

The normal mailing date is October 20 and the due date is December 20. Part payments are accepted until then. After the due date, interest builds monthly at the bank prime rate, and every 120 days adds another 5% penalty, ending at 20%. A balance left for a year grows noticeably, and any payoff quote goes stale fast.

  • Mobile homes: January mailing, April 1 due date, and a decal displayed after payment
  • Past April 1: a 10% filing penalty plus 1% monthly, then a FiFa on the clerk's docket and possible auction
  • A mobile home on land the owner holds can be homesteaded and is then taxed like real property

Mobile home dates differ between county pages, so call the Tax Commissioner to confirm yours before relying on April 1.

The base exemption deducts two thousand dollars from assessed value. It applies to county and school taxes but leaves out municipal school levies and bond debt.

File at the Tax Commissioner's counter from January 1 to April 1, between 8 and 5 on weekdays. State law grants no extension, so a missed date gives up the exemption for that year. Once approved it renews until your circumstances change, and it never exceeds the tax owed.

Three other programs cover land and buildings:

  • Conservation use and residential transitional property
  • Agricultural preferential assessment
  • Rehabilitated historic property

Each of those programs asks the owner to covenant with the Tax Assessor to maintain qualifying use for ten years or more. If you plan to sell enrolled land, phone (912) 375-6624 and ask what the covenant demands of a new owner.

Write to the Board of Tax Assessors within 45 days of the notice and name the appeal method you prefer. Notices for real and personal property usually go out in spring.

The county accepts four grounds: whether the property is taxable, its value, its uniformity with similar parcels, or a denied exemption. Objecting to the rate or the size of the bill does not qualify. A return filed between January 1 and April 1 can state your own January 1 opinion of market value and protects your appeal rights if the figure changes. Mobile home owners have 45 days from the bill mailing, then 21 days after a change notice to go before the Board of Equalization.

Owners return taxable property to the Tax Assessors Office from January 1 through April 1. When nothing is filed, last year's value and last year's real property exemptions carry over.

Appraisers use recent sales and market conditions as of January 1, and the spring notice states each parcel's value. A return of your own with a January 1 opinion keeps your appeal right alive if the figure is revised.

  • Tell the county about a new mailing address quickly, since notices follow the last one on file
  • Approved exemptions renew yearly until eligibility changes

Get a written payoff from the Tax Commissioner and have the closing office settle it out of your proceeds. Interest runs every month and penalties step up each 120 days, so an old quote may fall short. Ask for the figure close to the closing date.

The steps are short. Ask the commissioner for the payoff, ask the closing office to pay it from the seller's share, and keep the receipt. If a FiFa sits on the clerk's docket, it is public record and a title search will turn it up, so it has to be cleared before the deed can pass cleanly.

Timber land may owe timber tax, billed by the same office. If your mobile home sits on rented ground, confirm the decal and the April 1 bill before listing. A cash buyer skips lender appraisals and repair negotiations, but the payoff, the title search and the recorded deed still happen.

sections.h2: Refunds, city tax and recording tax
sections.html:
A refund is possible when tax was assessed or collected in error or illegally. Put the request in writing and start it within three years of payment. A refund that results from an appeal is handled as soon as the final taxable value is fixed.

Hazlehurst and Denton can levy their own ad valorem tax, and the city clerk normally bills it unless the city and county agreed to one combined bill. The county Tax Commissioner alone collects vehicle tax. State freeport rules let voters exempt commercial and industrial inventory, with applications due in the same window as returns.

When you buy or finance land, a long-term note secured by real estate has to be recorded within 90 days, and the state's recording tax is $1.50 for each $500 of face amount or fraction of it.

faqs.q: When is Jeff Davis County property tax due?
faqs.a: December 20. The usual mailing date is October 20, and partial payments are accepted up to the deadline.

faqs.q: How do I reach the Jeff Davis County Tax Commissioner?
faqs.a: Dial (912) 375-6622 or visit 14 Jeff Davis Street, Suite 104, in Hazlehurst. For valuation, phone the Tax Assessor at (912) 375-6624.

faqs.q: What does paying late cost in Jeff Davis County?
faqs.a: Monthly interest at the bank prime rate, plus 5% every 120 days up to a 20% cap. A mobile home paid after April 1 owes 10% plus 1% a month.

faqs.q: When can Jeff Davis County owners claim homestead?
faqs.a: From January 1 through April 1 for that tax year. Georgia law offers no extension.

faqs.q: What is the appeal deadline in Jeff Davis County?
faqs.a: Forty-five days from the notice date. Put the appeal in writing to the Board of Tax Assessors and state your method.
